operations.specification:
This endpoint allows new users to register accounts as todoListMember actors in the Todo List system. It creates a new todoListMember record using validated fields from the request body, most notably those corresponding to authentication data (such as email and password) as specified in the schema and requirements.

The operation ensures business constraints on email uniqueness and password strength as outlined in requirements. User data is validated before storage using rules defined on todo_list_todolistmembers for username/email/password. Successful registration returns JWT (access and refresh tokens) alongside account info.

This operation forms the entry point for regular users, mapping closely to the todo_list_todolistmembers Prisma table. Security considerations reflect only necessary information is accepted and no sensitive info (such as password hashes) is exposed in the response. All error handling (e.g., duplicate email, weak password) surfaces clear API errors.

Users who register via this endpoint will use this account for all future authentication actions. Related endpoints: /auth/todoListMember/login (for login), /auth/todoListMember/refresh (for token refresh). This operation is public and does not require authentication.
operations.description:
This API endpoint registers a new todoListMember (regular authenticated user) by creating a new record in the todo_list_todolistmembers table, using supplied registration information such as email, password, and other required authentication fields confirmed by schema. All required validations, such as unique email and password policy, are enforced at both the database and application logic levels.

Upon successful registration, the endpoint issues JWT access and refresh tokens through the ITodoListTodoListMember.IAuthorized DTO contract, with minimal user information. Security is carefully managed: only public-safe account details are returned, and sensitive data (e.g., password hashes) is never included in the payload. Failed registration attempts due to validation, duplication, or policy violation return precise errors referencing validation logic and schema/business rules.

This endpoint is directly related to the todo_list_todolistmembers Prisma DB table, reflecting its field requirements and unique constraints. Registration success implies immediate authentication via JWT. The security design restricts data visibility to the registering user only, safeguarding system integrity.

Future authentication flows (login and token refresh) depend on successful user creation here. Registration is the only entry for new todoListMember accounts.

Related endpoints: /auth/todoListMember/login for authentication, /auth/todoListMember/refresh for token renewal.
operations.summary: Register a new todoListMember account (todo_list_todolistmembers table) and issue initial JWT tokens.

requestBody.description: Registration data for new todoListMember. Must include all required fields for todo_list_todolistmembers as defined in the schema.

responseBody.description: Authorized user payload with tokens on successful registration.

operations.name: join

operations.specification:
This endpoint authenticates an existing todoListMember, validating credentials (email/username and password) provided in the request body. Successful authentication will issue new JWT access and refresh tokens, with payload structured according to ITodoListTodoListMember.IAuthorized (defined by the PascalCase service prefix and actor name pattern).

Validation includes checking for proper credentials, with account status verified in accordance with the todo_list_todolistmembers schema (e.g., active status, not disabled or removed). Password validation and comparison are executed securely, with no exposure of sensitive details in request or response.

If credentials are invalid, a precise error is returned. This endpoint is mapped strictly to the todo_list_todolistmembers table and interacts only with confirmed schema fields.

This operation is the main login entry for regular users. Related endpoints: /auth/todoListMember/join (registration), /auth/todoListMember/refresh (token refresh).
operations.description:
Authenticate a todoListMember by verifying their credentials (such as email and password) against the todo_list_todolistmembers table. Only actors with valid, existing accounts in the table and proper credentials will be authenticated. Secure password comparison, account state checks, and validation error handling are all built using schema-enforced fields.

JWT tokens (access and refresh) are issued upon successful login through the ITodoListTodoListMember.IAuthorized DTO. No sensitive authentication data is ever returned in the payload; only session-safe and necessary user information is included.

Account lockout, password retry limitations, and disabling policies are enforced as per schema and requirements; failures always provide clear error responses indicating reason for denial, referencing both business and DB rules.

This endpoint is directly dependent on successful registration using /auth/todoListMember/join, and it must work in concert with the refresh endpoint for token renewal. The login operation is public and does not require prior authentication.
operations.summary: Authenticate a todoListMember using credentials and issue JWT tokens (todo_list_todolistmembers table).

requestBody.description: Login credentials for todoListMember account (must include fields validated in schema, such as email and password).

responseBody.description: Authorized user payload with tokens on successful authentication.

operations.name: login

operations.specification:
This endpoint refreshes JWT tokens for a logged-in todoListMember using an existing, non-expired refresh token provided in the request body. The operation securely validates the refresh token against the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table (or its equivalent), ensuring the token is unexpired, untampered, and mapped to an active todoListMember account.

The process is tied to the session schema structure, following all field-level validation as specified by the schema for refresh tokens and session management. Security checks include issuing new access and refresh tokens if the old token is valid and unrevoked, and denying requests with invalid token states.

This endpoint is strictly related to authentication session management and does not expose any additional user information. Participation in this operation requires a valid current refresh token in the request body: unauthorized or expired tokens result in immediate failure and error reporting.

This endpoint depends on prior registration/login operations for token issuance, and complements the system's secure session handling workflows.
operations.description:
Refresh JWT tokens for an authenticated todoListMember session. The endpoint uses the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table to validate the provided refresh token (checking for existence, expiry, revocation, and association with an active todoListMember account) before issuing new tokens. All relevant validation and session management rules are enforced at both schema and application levels.

A valid, non-expired refresh token is required in the request body; invalid or revoked tokens will fail securely with a clear error response. No user account or sensitive session state is returned except new tokens (as ITodoListTodoListMember.IAuthorized contract). The entire workflow matches business and system security requirements for session renewal.

Credential compromise and replay attack risks are mitigated based on field-verified logic enforced in the session schema, and only accounts in active state may obtain refreshed tokens through this endpoint.

This operation should be used in conjunction with /auth/todoListMember/login and /auth/todoListMember/join endpoints for a complete authentication lifecycle.

Related resources include the underlying todo_list_todolistmember_sessions schema.
operations.summary: Refresh JWT tokens for an authenticated todoListMember using the session table.

requestBody.description: Refresh token payload (must match schema-defined fields for token validation).

responseBody.description: Authorized user payload with new tokens after refresh.

operations.name: refresh

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the currently authenticated user's account details (todoListMember) in the minimal Todo List system. It is bound to the todo_list_todolistmembers table and returns the user's own private account profile, including email and creation timestamp, with security best practices (never exposes password_hash). This endpoint is strictly self-service and requires a valid authenticated session. All information returned pertains only to the current user—no user or administrator may access other users' account records. The operation does not accept parameters or a request body.
operations.description:
Retrieve the authenticated user's account information in the Todo List application.

This endpoint provides the current todoListMember with their account details, such as email and account creation date, directly from the todo_list_todolistmembers table. The response excludes sensitive data like the password hash, complying with privacy and security requirements.

Access to this operation is strictly limited to the authenticated session's user. Attempts to access this endpoint without authentication result in an error, and unauthorized attempts to access another user's data are prevented by business logic and session validation. There is no administrative override or sharing; every account is strictly personal.

This operation integrates with business rules enforcing strict data isolation. It should be used by frontends for displaying user profile information or confirming successful login. Related endpoints include updating personal account information or deleting one's account.
operations.summary: Retrieve authenticated user's todoListMember profile from the database.

responseBody.description: Authenticated user's account details (excluding sensitive fields).

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation updates the current authenticated user's account information (todoListMember) as stored in the todo_list_todolistmembers table. The operation supports editing only allowed fields (such as email, subject to uniqueness), and never allows updating the password or other sensitive attributes through this endpoint. Users may update their email, which must remain unique, and the operation enforces all schema validation constraints. Password updates and account deletion are handled by separate business processes/services. Only the currently authenticated user may invoke this endpoint, and the changes apply exclusively to their account; there is no provision for updating other users' records or performing bulk or administrative updates.
operations.description:
Update the email address associated with the authenticated user's todoListMember account.

This endpoint processes requests from the logged-in user to change their own email address, as long as the new email conforms to uniqueness and format rules defined in the todo_list_todolistmembers table. All other fields are either immutable via this endpoint or handled through dedicated flows.

Ownership is strictly enforced by session validation. Attempts to update other attributes (e.g., password) or other users' data via this endpoint are rejected at both the API level and in the business logic. The system ensures the requested email remains unique, and changes trigger the appropriate updated_at timestamp. Security and privacy best practices ensure sensitive data is never accepted or returned.

Related operations for password or account deletion are implemented separately. This update flow requires authentication and only affects the session owner's data.
operations.summary: Update authenticated user's todoListMember account email.

requestBody.description: New email address to update for the authenticated user's own account. Must be unique and valid.

responseBody.description: Updated account information for the authenticated todoListMember user.

operations.name: update

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes the currently authenticated user's account from the todo_list_todolistmembers table. All associated data, including the user's todo items and session records, is irreversibly removed in accordance with system requirements and business rules. Account deletion enforces immediate loss of access and guarantees that no personal or todo data remains post-operation.
operations.description:
Delete the currently authenticated todo list member account and all personal data.

This operation allows a user to permanently erase their own account from the application, securing irreversible removal of their personal data, todo items, and all session information. Once deleted, the account and all associated resources become unrecoverable.

Security enforcement strictly ensures that users can only delete their own account by verifying authentication and ownership and that the operation cannot be triggered for other users' accounts. The system ensures compliance with data privacy and erasure regulations.

This endpoint is critical for user autonomy and privacy, and must enforce that account deletion triggers cascading removal of all related items and sessions. Post-deletion, the user is immediately signed out and must register anew to use the service again.
operations.summary: Permanently delete the authenticated todo list member's account (todo_list_todolistmembers table).
operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation retrieves a paginated list of session records (from todo_list_todolistmember_sessions) belonging to the currently authenticated todoListMember. Sessions represent login activities from various devices or browsers. The data includes creation timestamp, session details, and expiration status. The endpoint supports search, filtering, and pagination and is strictly scoped to the owner.
operations.description:
Retrieve all session records for the currently authenticated todo list member in a paginated list format.

This operation enables users to review their login and session activity history, including current and prior device/browser logins, helping them recognize authorized and unauthorized access. Results are ordered by session creation time and may be filtered or paged as necessary for audit or comfort.

Access is restricted to the owning todoListMember; no user or admin can query sessions for others. The operation adheres to business rules on session management and privacy. Typical use includes displaying session information for user awareness and security controls, such as disconnecting devices manually (not part of this minimal endpoint).
operations.summary: Retrieve all sessions for the authenticated todo list member (todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table).

requestBody.description: Query and pagination parameters for fetching user sessions.

responseBody.description: Paginated list of the authenticated user's session records.

operations.name: index

operations.specification:
Retrieves detailed information about a specific authentication session for the currently authenticated user. This operation queries the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table to provide information such as session creation time, device and IP details, referrer context, and current status (active or expired). The session must belong to the requesting user (as enforced by ownership in the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions model referencing todoListTodolistmember). 

This endpoint is essential for users to audit their login activity on various devices and browsers, helping detect unauthorized access and monitor security. Only the owner of the session may retrieve its details, and authentication is required for access. The returned information includes timestamps, location/IP, device context, and validity status.

The operation does not expose authentication secrets; only context and status information is returned. Attempts to retrieve sessions that do not belong to the user or do not exist for their account will be rejected with appropriate error handling. Related endpoints include session deletion for immediate revocation and list endpoints for session enumeration.
operations.description:
Retrieve detailed authentication session information for the current user from the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table.

This operation allows an authenticated user to view information about a particular active or historical session on their account. Details provided include the session's creation time, IP address, connection context, and referrer. Users can use this information to audit their account for unauthorized or unusual activity.

Access control is strictly enforced; users cannot retrieve sessions belonging to other accounts. Strong rate limiting and auditing are applied to prevent abuse. If a session is expired, this operation will still return historic context, but indicate the invalidation timestamp if present. Attempts to retrieve a nonexistent session or session not owned by the user are met with permission-denied or not-found errors.

To enumerate all sessions, a list endpoint (not included here) would be used; for revoking a session, use the DELETE endpoint for the same resource path.
operations.summary: Retrieve authentication session details for a specific session owned by the current user (todo_list_todolistmember_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the authentication session to retrieve. Must belong to the current authenticated user.

responseBody.description: Detailed session information for the specified authentication session owned by the current user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification:
Deletes (revokes) a specific authentication session from the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table for the current authenticated user. This operation ends the session with immediate effect, preventing further use of the corresponding token or session credentials. Action is allowed only if the session belongs to the requester, as confirmed via the todo_list_todolistmember_id foreign key. 

Session deletion enables users to remotely log out from individual devices or browsers, particularly useful for removing stale, lost, or suspicious sessions for security reasons. This operation guarantees immediate invalidation of future requests with the deleted session's credentials, though historic audit information may still be retained for compliance. No sensitive credentials are exposed or returned.

Attempts to delete sessions not owned by the requester, or sessions that do not exist for their account, are met with permission-denied or not-found errors. Related endpoints include GET for querying session information and PATCH lists for enumerating or bulk-managing sessions.
operations.description:
Revoke (delete) a specific authentication session for the current user from the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions table.

This operation immediately ends a session associated with the current authenticated user, providing a security mechanism to force logout from previously active devices or browsers. It is commonly used when a user suspects their account has been accessed from an unauthorized location or device, or to perform regular security hygiene.

Strict access control ensures users cannot delete sessions they do not own. The session is immediately unavailable for authentication, but a record may remain for audit or compliance purposes. Attempts to revoke a nonexistent or non-owned session are handled with clear error messages and appropriate logging for security monitoring. Users should follow up with GET on the same path to verify session expiration if needed.
operations.summary: Revoke (delete) an authentication session for the current user (todo_list_todolistmember_sessions).

parameters.name: sessionId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the authentication session to revoke. Must belong to the current authenticated user.

operations.name: erase

operations.specification: This operation searches and retrieves a paginated list of todo items belonging exclusively to the authenticated todoListMember. It operates on the todo_list_todos table, enforcing per-user isolation via the todo_list_todolistmembers relation and the unique index on (todo_list_todolistmember_id, title). The operation supports advanced filtering (by completion status, creation or due date ranges), sorting, and pagination based on business rules (e.g., max 1000 todos per user, rate limit 30 creations/minute, only access to own todos allowed). The output is always scoped to the requesting user's data and adheres to all field validation requirements from the schema.
operations.description:
Retrieve a filtered and paginated list of the authenticated user's todo items, including support for filtering by completion status, date ranges, and search terms on title or description.

This operation strictly enforces per-user data boundaries as described in the prisma schema and requirements analysis. Only the currently authenticated todoListMember can retrieve their own todos; no collaborative or administrative listing is permitted. The operation validates that pagination and filter queries adhere to business rules, such as creation and update date ordering, and rate limiting.

The todo_list_todos schema mandates field validation: title (1-100 chars, unique per user), description (up to 1000 chars), is_complete (boolean), and timestamps. Clients may sort results and filter by these properties as allowed. All response data is guaranteed to be owned by the authenticated user and paginated for performance and quota enforcement. If no todos exist for the user, an empty, but paginated, result is returned.
operations.summary: Search and retrieve a paginated list of personal todo_list_todos records for the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Advanced search, filter, sort, and pagination parameters for retrieving the authenticated user's todo items.

responseBody.description: Paginated page of todo summary information results for the authenticated todoListMember.

operations.name: index

operations.specification: This operation retrieves the detailed information for a specific todo item owned by the authenticated todoListMember. It operates on the todo_list_todos table, using the id (UUID) primary key to identify the record and the foreign key todo_list_todolistmember_id to ensure privacy and single-user scope. Permission logic ensures that no user can view or access any todo belonging to another member. All validation and error handling follow business rules and schema requirements, including field limits and ownership checks.
operations.description:
Retrieve complete details of a single todo item by its unique identifier, strictly limited to the authenticated user's own data as defined by the todo_list_todos Prisma schema.

Access is permitted only if the todo's todo_list_todolistmember_id matches the current session; otherwise, a clear error is returned as per requirements. The response includes all fields: title, description, is_complete, timestamps, and completed_at as applicable. Attempting to retrieve another user's todo or a non-existent ID results in a permission or not found error, with no data leakage.

All business constraints from the requirements are enforced, including: field validation, ownership, and the irreversibility of deletions (no recovery for removed items). The operation forms part of the minimal CRUD suite for personal todo management.
operations.summary: Retrieve detailed information for a specific todo_list_todos record owned by the authenticated user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo (owned by the authenticated todoListMember).

responseBody.description: Detailed complete todo item record matching the requested id if owned by the authenticated user.

operations.name: at

operations.specification: This operation creates a new todo item for the authenticated user in the Todo List application. The todo_list_todos table is the authoritative data store for all actionable tasks where each todo is private and owned by a single user (referenced via the todo_list_todolistmembers table). Each todo requires a unique title per user, an optional description, and supports marking the todo as complete immediately on creation if desired. The service applies business rules enforcing per-user title uniqueness, valid text input ranges, and automatically sets timestamps for creation and update. The operation returns the full detail of the newly created todo, as persisted to the database.
operations.description:
Create a new todo item for the authenticated user. This endpoint allows a user to add a new task to their private collection of todos. Each todo must have a unique title (per user) and may include an optional longer description along with its initial completion status (which defaults to incomplete if omitted).

Only the owner can create todos; there is no support for public, shared, or admin-managed task creation. Security is strictly enforced through authentication, ensuring users cannot create todos for other accounts. The timestamps for creation and the most recent update are set server-side and are not client-modifiable.

Input validation checks title length (1-100 characters, non-blank), optional description (up to 1000 characters), and that initial completion status is boolean. Uniqueness of a todo’s title is enforced at both business and database layer for every individual user. Related endpoints include updating and deleting todos (by ID) which also require strict ownership.
operations.summary: Create a new todo in the todo_list_todos table for the authenticated user.

requestBody.description: Creation payload for a new todo, including unique title, optional description, and initial completion status.

responseBody.description: The complete detail of the created todo as persisted to the database.

operations.name: create

operations.specification: This operation updates an existing todo record belonging to the authenticated user. Targeting the todo_list_todos table, it supports editing the title (with enforcement of per-user uniqueness), updating the description, and changing the completion status or completion timestamp. The todoId path parameter is the required unique identifier for the specific todo; only the owner may update their own todos. The update logic applies auditing of updated_at timestamp, and sets completed_at automatically when marking as complete. All validations on input (length, allowed values, uniqueness) are strictly enforced.
operations.description:
Update the details of an existing todo item that belongs to the authenticated user. This includes changing its title (which must remain unique for the user), updating its description, or toggling completion status. The completed_at field will be set or cleared automatically based on is_complete status.

The endpoint requires authentication and only allows the todo’s actual owner to apply updates. Security and data isolation are enforced through user-token verification and strict ownership checks. All input fields are validated according to business logic and Prisma schema constraints; no cross-user updates or admin overrides are allowed.

If the title is updated, it must not duplicate another of the user's todos. The operation automatically updates timestamps for auditability and preserves referential integrity to the owning user.
operations.summary: Update an existing todo in the todo_list_todos table, identified by todoId, for the authenticated user.

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: The unique identifier (UUID) of the todo to update, as assigned at creation.

requestBody.description: Full or partial update data for the todo, including new title, description, and/or completion status.

responseBody.description: The todo after all requested updates are applied.

operations.name: update

prerequisites.description: A todo item must be created by the authenticated user before it can be updated using its unique todoId.

operations.specification: This operation permanently deletes a specific todo item from the system. It directly manipulates the 'todo_list_todos' table in the database, and is intended for use by authenticated users to remove their own todos. The deletion is a hard removal—once executed, the todo and its data are permanently erased from the database with no recovery mechanism. The operation verifies ownership by matching the authenticated user's identity to the owner of the todo item in accordance with application-level security logic. Only the creator/owner of the todo item is allowed to delete it. All business logic and constraints relevant to this action are enforced in the provider logic utilizing the schema, including any relational constraint handling or checks for children resources. This deletion action does not affect user authentication or system-managed logs, and only applies for user-generated todo items.
operations.description:
Delete a specific todo item from the Todo List application.

This operation allows an authenticated user to permanently remove a todo item identified by its unique identifier. Upon invocation, the system performs an authorization check to ensure that only the owner of the todo may execute this operation. The deletion is irreversible; all data associated with the todo is removed from persistent storage, and there is no soft delete or recovery provided. The operation enforces all validation and business rules defined by the 'todo_list_todos' table schema, including checks for foreign key integrity and any additional deletion prerequisites.

Security is enforced at the application service layer, requiring the authenticated user to be the owner of the target todo. No data is returned if the deletion is successful, and clients should handle both success and any failure conditions (such as attempting to delete a non-existent or inaccessible todo) according to standard error response patterns. This endpoint operates independently of the authentication/session mechanism, focusing solely on todo resource cleanup within a member's list.
operations.summary: Permanently remove a specific todo from the authenticated user's list (todo_list_todos table)

parameters.name: todoId
parameters.description: Unique identifier of the target todo item belonging to the Todo List application member

operations.name: erase

prerequisites.description: A todo item must exist before it can be permanently deleted. Use the POST /todoList/todoListMember/todos operation to create the todo before deletion is attempted.

authorizations.name: todoListMember
authorizations.description: Authenticated individual user who can create, view, update, and delete their own Todo items. Has access only to their own data and basic user features. Cannot access or manage other users' data or system settings.

limit.description: Limitation of records per a page.

pages.description:
Total pages.

Equal to {@link records} / {@link limit} with ceiling.

access.description:
JWT access token for authenticated requests.

This token should be included in the Authorization header for subsequent
authenticated API requests as `Bearer {token}`.

refresh.description:
Refresh token for obtaining new access tokens.

This token can be used to request new access tokens when the current access
token expires, extending the user's session.

expired_at.description:
Access token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating when the access token will expire and
can no longer be used for authentication.

refreshable_until.description:
Refresh token expiration timestamp.

ISO 8601 date-time string indicating the latest time until which the
refresh token can be used to obtain new access tokens.

IAuthorizationToken.description:
Authorization token response structure.

This interface defines the structure of the authorization token response
returned after successful user authentication. It contains both access and
refresh tokens along with their expiration information.

This token structure is automatically included in API schemas when the system
detects authorization actors in the requirements analysis phase. It provides
a standard format for JWT-based authentication across the generated backend
applications.

IPageITodoListTodolistmemberSession.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

IPageITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
A page.

Collection of records with pagination information.

id.description: Primary Key. Unique identifier for this session instance. Assigned by the database when the session record is created and used throughout the system to refer to this session.

member.description: References the todoListMember who owns this session. Always a BELONGS-TO .ISummary object, not a raw UUID, for reference integrity and UI context.

ip.description: IP address from which the session was created or last accessed. Used for audit and security monitoring. Immutable for the duration of the session. Must be a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address string.

href.description: Connection URL or origin used when session was initialized. Provides client-side context on the origin of session establishment.

referrer.description: Referrer value (if present) at the time of login or session creation; used for security and audit context.

created_at.description: Timestamp when the session was initially created. Set by the system upon session establishment.

expired_at.description: Timestamp marking when the session was invalidated (logged out, timed out, or revoked). If null, the session is currently active.

ITodoListTodolistmemberSession.description:
Authentication sessions for a todoListMember.

Represents a unique session established for a todoListMember, mapping to a login by a specific browser or device. Records IP, session creation details, and session lifetime context for auditing and device management. Session ownership is always expressed by a BELONGS-TO relation modeled as a .ISummary object reference (member).

page.description: The page number to retrieve in paginated query of sessions. Must be positive integer; page 1 is default. Used for limiting results and browsing session history.

limit.description: Maximum number of session records to return per page. Used to control response payload size and client-side result batching. Must be between 1 and 100.

ITodoListTodolistmemberSession.IRequest.description:
Request parameters for searching and paginating session records for the authenticated todoListMember.

Clients can specify pagination information to retrieve subsets of session activity efficiently. This is used for secure audit and session management UIs.

ITodoListTodo.description: Represents a single todo item in the Todo List application, privately owned and managed by the authenticated user who created it.

id.description: Unique identifier of the todo item. Serves as the primary key. Must be a valid version 4 UUID.

title.description: The title of the todo, as provided by its creator. Must be unique per user, minimum 1 and maximum 100 characters, non-blank.

oneOf.description: Optional longer details or notes for the todo. Maximum 1000 characters. Nullable.
Null if no description is provided.

description.description: Optional longer details or notes for the todo. Maximum 1000 characters. Nullable.

is_complete.description: Completion status of the todo. True if marked complete; false if still pending or in progress.

oneOf.description: Timestamp when todo was marked complete, if applicable.
Null if not completed yet.

completed_at.description: Timestamp when todo was marked complete, or null if incomplete.

created_at.description: Timestamp for when the todo was created.

updated_at.description: Timestamp for the most recent update to the todo, including edits or status changes.

ITodoListTodo.IRequest.description: Parameters for advanced search, filtering, sorting, and pagination when querying the authenticated user's todo items.

oneOf.description: A search term to match against todo titles and descriptions, case-insensitive.
Omit or set to null to disable free-text search.

searchTerm.description: A search term to match against todo titles and descriptions, case-insensitive.

oneOf.description: If set, filters todos by completion status (true for completed, false for pending/in progress).
Unset or null to include both complete and incomplete todos.

is_complete.description: If set, filters todos by completion status (true for completed, false for pending/in progress).

oneOf.description: Lower bound (inclusive) of creation timestamp for filtering todos, as ISO8601 datetime.
Omit or set to null to disable lower bound filter.

created_from.description: Lower bound (inclusive) of creation timestamp for filtering todos, as ISO8601 datetime.

oneOf.description: Upper bound (inclusive) of creation timestamp for filtering todos, as ISO8601 datetime.
Omit or set to null to disable upper bound filter.

created_to.description: Upper bound (inclusive) of creation timestamp for filtering todos, as ISO8601 datetime.

oneOf.description: Sort field to order results by. Only 'created_at' (default) or 'title' are allowed.
Sort field to order results by. Only 'created_at' (default) or 'title' are allowed.
Omit or set to null to use default sort option (created_at DESC).

sort_by.description: Sort field to order results by. Only 'created_at' (default) or 'title' are allowed.

oneOf.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending (default).
Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending (default).
Unset or null uses default 'desc'.

sort_order.description: Sort order direction. 'asc' for ascending, 'desc' for descending (default).

page.description: Page number in result set (starting from 1). Default 1. Supports up to 1000 pages (max 1000 todos per user).

page_size.description: Number of todos to return per page. Default is 20. Maximum is 100. Excessive values result in error.

title.description: Todo title provided by the owner. Must be unique for each user, between 1 and 100 characters, and non-blank.

oneOf.description: Optional longer details or notes for the todo. Allows up to 1000 characters. Can be null or empty as needed.
No description provided.

description.description: Optional longer details or notes for the todo. Allows up to 1000 characters. Can be null or empty as needed.

is_complete.description: Completion status. True if the todo is marked complete, false if still pending or in progress.

ITodoListTodo.ICreate.description:
DTO for creating a new todo item owned by the authenticated user (todo_list_todos).

Title must be unique per user and within 1-100 characters. Description is optional, up to 1000 chars. Completion status may be specified at creation; defaults to false if omitted at service layer. Owner ID is always injected from authentication context, never provided by the client.

All timestamps and authority fields are managed by the backend. Irreversible deletion is enforced per business rule. Security ensures strict user isolation: only the authenticated user may create todos for themselves.

title.description: Updated todo title, if changed. Must remain unique for each user, between 1 and 100 characters.

oneOf.description: Updated description. Optional and can be set to null/empty.
Remove description or leave unset.

description.description: Updated longer details or notes for the todo. Optional; can be set to null or omitted.

is_complete.description: Set to true if marking todo as complete; false if marking as incomplete. Triggers automatic update of completed_at field.

ITodoListTodo.IUpdate.description:
DTO for updating an existing todo item owned by the authenticated user (todo_list_todos).

Used in update operations (PUT/PATCH) where any combination of title, description, or completion status may be modified.
All fields are optional—supply only those being changed, but must still comply with per-user title uniqueness and validation rules.

Strict owner/todo linkage is enforced by the service layer, with all user identity and authority injected from the authentication context.

ITodoListTodo.ISummary.description:
Summary representation of a Todo item for list and overview endpoints in the Todo List application.

This schema presents only the most essential properties needed to display, filter, and interact with todo items in list or reference views. Verbose fields such as "description" or audit timestamps are intentionally omitted to optimize payload efficiency and uphold privacy.

Each summary is strictly private to its owner (the authenticated todo_list_todolistmember), ensuring per-user isolation. The summary omits foreign/user identifiers, further reinforcing security boundaries for all users. This structure is recommended for pagination, dashboard, and status filter contexts.

id.description: System-generated unique identifier for the todo item, following UUID v4 standards. Used as the canonical reference in API calls and for establishing robust foreign key relationships across models. This property is immutable after creation.

title.description: Short title of the todo, created and managed by its owner. Must be unique per user, non-blank, and within 1-100 characters in length, as enforced by both business rules and the database unique index. Used for display, quick navigation, and user task organization.

is_complete.description: Indicates completion status: true if the todo is marked finished, false if still active or in progress. Used for filtering, batch operations, and UI status indication. Business logic may restrict editing for completed items.

oneOf.description: ISO 8601 timestamp recording when the todo was marked complete. Set at the moment of transition from incomplete to complete.
Null means the todo is still in progress and has not yet been completed. No timestamp is stored until completion occurs.

completed_at.description: The date and time the todo was marked complete. Null if completion has not occurred. Used for audit, reporting, and workflow tracking.

ITodoListTodolistmember.ICreate.description:
Create DTO for registering a new todoListMember account.

Represents user-supplied data required to create a new account in the Todo List system. Fields correspond directly to the todo_list_todolistmembers Prisma model, but exclude password hash and system/timestamp fields. Email must be unique for each user, following RFC 5322 and application-specific email requirements, and is used for both authentication and password recovery. The password field holds the plain-text password for account creation, which is hashed securely by the backend; validation rules (length, complexity) follow business rules specified in requirements. 

The DTO includes session context fields for self-signup, as mandated for authentication flows in atomic operation requirements: 'href' (the URL from which the signup is performed) and 'referrer' (the Referrer HTTP header), both required. The 'ip' can be supplied by the client or derived by the server, and is optional.

Ownership fields, id, created_at, and password_hash are excluded as they are system-managed or come from authentication context. No other actor or reference fields are present, as Todo List is a single-user, non-delegated model.

email.description: User's unique email used for authentication and communication. Must be a valid RFC 5322 email address. Uniqueness and format validated server-side.

password.description: Plain-text password for registration, to be hashed by the backend. Must meet minimum security requirements (length, complexity). Not stored or transmitted after initial use.

href.description: The client page URL from which signup is performed. Provides session context. Required for self-signup according to system requirements.

referrer.description: Referrer URL (from HTTP Referrer header) present at the time of signup. Provides additional session context. Required for self-signup.

oneOf.description: Client's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6 format) for session tracking. Optional: will be extracted by server if omitted.
Client's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6 format) for session tracking. Optional: will be extracted by server if omitted.
Field can be omitted or explicitly set to null when not supplied.

ip.description: Client's IP address (IPv4 or IPv6) for session context in authentication. Optional; provided by client or derived by server. Will be stored with the session if available.

ITodoListTodolistmember.IAuthorized.description:
Authorization result DTO after successful join or login for todoListMember.

Returned by both account registration and login endpoints. Contains the user's unique id, a JWT token information object, and the minimal account data required to support client authorization state. No sensitive credential or password information is ever included in this DTO. 

The 'id' field is a system-generated UUID corresponding to the todoListMember's primary key. The 'token' is an authorization token object containing access and refresh JWT tokens and related metadata, always returned after successful auth. 

No account or actor context beyond the self-user is present, as the system prevents all cross-user access. No properties are included from the password_hash or other credential-bearing fields. Other fields (such as name) would be included only if present in the DB schema, but for this minimal user model, only the id is returned aside from the token.

id.description: Unique identifier for the authenticated todoListMember. System-managed UUID from the todo_list_todolistmembers table.

email.description:
Unique email address used for authentication and communication with the todoListMember.

Must comply with proper email format requirements and is uniquely enforced within the system. The email is required both for login and for handling account recovery processes. Changing the email is handled through dedicated endpoints ensuring uniqueness is maintained.

created_at.description:
Date and time when the todoListMember account was created.

Represents the timestamp of account creation and is used for audit trails and compliance purposes. This is an immutable value and is automatically assigned when the account is first registered. Provided in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-11-17T15:25:14.066Z).

email.description: Unique user email address for authentication and communication. Must follow proper email format and is used for login and password reset.

password.description: The plain text password supplied by the user for authentication. Must be at least 8 characters long. This value will be validated but is never stored as plain text; only the password hash is retained by the system.

href.description: The URL from which the login request was initiated (current page address). Provides full context for session creation, audit, and security. Required for session recording.

referrer.description: The referrer URL at the time of login (typically the previous page or HTTP referer). Used for session audit trails and context.

ip.description: Client IP address as observed by the client or extracted from request metadata. Used for security and auditing. Optional: if not provided, the server will attempt to detect automatically.

ITodoListTodolistmember.ILogin.description:
Login credentials for a todoListMember account. The client must provide a valid email and password for authentication, along with session context fields for audit and security purposes. The href and referrer fields are required for session creation and audit trail.

This schema strictly maps to the todo_list_todolistmembers table for credential validation and ensures that password handling and session context are securely managed.

refresh_token.description: Refresh token previously issued to the client for session continuation. This token is validated against active authentication sessions and must be unexpired, valid, and associated with an existing todoListMember account.

ITodoListTodolistmember.IRefresh.description:
Request schema to refresh JWT tokens for a todoListMember session. The client must provide a valid refresh_token, which is validated against the session table to confirm activity status, expiry, and association with a valid account.

Directly references the todo_list_todolistmember_sessions Prisma table for its field structure and validation constraints.

id.description:
Unique identifier for the todoListMember account.

Serves as the primary key in the database and is used for all references to this account throughout the Todo List system. The value is generated upon account creation and is globally unique. Never changes once assigned and is used for data integrity, session management, and auditing.

email.description:
Unique email address used for authentication and communication with the todoListMember.

Must comply with proper email format requirements and is uniquely enforced within the system. The email is required both for login and for handling account recovery processes. Changing the email is handled through dedicated endpoints ensuring uniqueness is maintained.

created_at.description:
Date and time when the todoListMember account was created.

Represents the timestamp of account creation and is used for audit trails and compliance purposes. This is an immutable value and is automatically assigned when the account is first registered. Provided in ISO 8601 format (e.g., 2025-11-17T15:25:14.066Z).

ITodoListTodolistmember.description:
Minimal todoListMember account profile entity for the Todo List application.

Represents an individual authenticated user of the system. Includes the user's unique identifier, email address, and the timestamp of account creation. Excludes all sensitive fields such as password_hash, complying with security and privacy best practices.

Returned by authentication-protected endpoints to display the account profile of the currently logged-in user. Directly maps to the todo_list_todolistmembers table in the underlying database. Used exclusively for self-service access and NEVER exposes another user's data.

email.description:
New email address for the todoListMember account.

Must be unique across all registered users and conform to valid email format. Updating this field changes the email used for both login and communication. Email changes are validated for uniqueness and proper formatting before being accepted. Other fields such as password may only be updated through dedicated operations and are not permitted in this schema.

ITodoListTodolistmember.IUpdate.description:
Schema for updating the authenticated todoListMember's email address.

Allows the logged-in user to update their own account's email field, provided the new value is unique and valid. All other account fields (such as password or ID) are immutable or managed by separate flows. Directly maps to the email property of the todo_list_todolistmembers table and enforces database-level uniqueness constraints. This schema is only used in authenticated self-service endpoints where the actor is updating their own information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the todoListMember, system-assigned UUID v4. Serves as the stable reference for foreign keys, audit tracking, and access control across all member-owned entities.

email.description: Primary email address for the todoListMember user account. Used for authentication, display in user-facing contexts, and notification delivery. Must be a valid, unique email within the system.

ITodoListTodolistmember.ISummary.description:
Minimal summary DTO for a todoListMember entity.

This schema is typically used as a reference in other objects (such as foreign key associations in ITodoListTodo) and in member selection UIs or audit logs. It contains only the profile fields needed for display, authorization tracking, and relational integrity in summary or belongs-to contexts.
